title: The Power of Communication
summary: Discover how words, gestures and voice work together in everyday communication.
keyIdeas: Verbal communication uses spoken or written words. Non-verbal communication includes gestures, facial expressions, posture and sounds without words.
Body language and tone can support words and help make a message clear. Their meaning depends on the person and the context.
Active listening means paying attention, letting others speak and responding to their message. Not everyone needs eye contact to listen.

activities.prompt: Is this statement correct? 'Verbal communication only includes words spoken aloud; written texts are non-verbal communication.'
activities.explanation: False. Verbal communication uses words, whether spoken or written.

activities.prompt: Sort these actions by the main type of communication they use.
activities.explanation: Emails, spoken podcasts and phone conversations use words. Gestures, facial expressions and sounds without words are non-verbal.

items.text: An email to organise a group project
Raising a thumb to show that something went well
A spoken podcast episode about inventions from history
The sound of an ambulance siren in the street
Frowning when an explanation is unclear
A phone conversation with your grandmother

activities.prompt: Match each action to its main non-verbal feature.
activities.explanation: Non-verbal communication includes facial expressions, voice qualities beyond the words (paralanguage), posture and physical distance (proxemics).

pairs.left: Lowering your voice and slowing its pace
Crossing your arms and turning your back
Respecting personal space during a conversation

activities.prompt: Hugo gives a science presentation with clear words, but looks down and speaks very quietly. Which change would help his audience?
activities.explanation: An audible voice helps people follow. Hugo can face the group or look at a nearby point if that is more comfortable; direct eye contact is not essential.
activities.hint: Think about what helps the audience hear and follow his explanation.
options: Speaking as quickly as possible to finish sooner.
Memorising the text so he never uses his notes.
Speaking at an audible volume and directing his explanation towards the audience.

activities.prompt: Complete the Spanish sentence with the most precise word.
activities.explanation: Coherence means that the words, gestures and tone support the same message rather than contradicting one another.
activities.sentence: Cuando las palabras que decimos coinciden con lo que transmiten nuestros gestos, existe una clara ___ entre el mensaje verbal y el no verbal.
options: coherencia
contradicción
separación

activities.prompt: In which situation might the gestures make us wonder whether the words reflect the person's feelings?
activities.explanation: A shaking voice and a frown might seem at odds with saying everything is fine. Gestures cannot tell us someone's feelings for certain: ask respectfully.
options: Adrián says he is absolutely fine while looking down, frowning and speaking with a shaking voice.
Lucía says she is delighted to see someone, with a big smile and open arms.
Aisha quietly raises her hand and waits for the teacher to let her speak.

activities.prompt: Put these steps for a respectful contribution to a formal debate in order.
activities.explanation: Ask for a turn and wait for it, then explain your reasons and listen to the response.
items: Ask for a turn to speak.
Wait for your turn and prepare your contribution.
Explain your reasons calmly, with suitable pauses.
Listen to the response without interrupting.

activities.prompt: Read the Spanish text about the school debate and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: The story shows how words and non-verbal features can work together in clear and respectful communication.
activities.title: Más allá de las palabras
activities.text:
En el colegio Los Olivos, Martina y Leo preparaban la final del torneo de debate. Martina dominaba los datos y los argumentos, pero en los ensayos solía cruzarse de brazos y mirar al techo cada vez que su oponente intervenía. Su tutora, Elena, le explicó que la comunicación no termina cuando dejamos de hablar: la postura de escucha transmite tanto respeto como las palabras.

Por su parte, Leo hablaba con entusiasmo, pero gesticulaba de forma tan exagerada y rápida que distraía al tribunal. Ambos decidieron corregir estos detalles. En el debate definitivo, Martina escuchó a su rival manteniendo la mirada atenta y asintiendo con la cabeza, mientras que Leo moderó sus gestos para enfatizar solo las ideas clave. Gracias a esa armonía entre su discurso verbal y su lenguaje corporal, el equipo transmitió seguridad y logró convencer al jurado.

questions.prompt: Which habit did Martina need to work on during rehearsals?
questions.explanation: The text says she crossed her arms and looked at the ceiling whenever her opponent spoke.
options: She crossed her arms and looked at the ceiling while her opponent spoke.
She spoke so quietly that nobody could hear her reasons.
She kept her eyes closed throughout her contribution.

questions.prompt: According to the text, why can posture matter while listening?
questions.explanation: The text presents listening posture as one way to communicate attention and respect. People can show active listening in different ways.
options: It can show respect for the speaker and active listening.
It automatically makes us remember everything the speaker says.
Debate rules forbid moving any part of the body.

questions.prompt: What can we conclude from Martina and Leo's experience?
questions.explanation: Clear reasons and non-verbal communication suited to the situation can work together to help the audience follow.
options: Knowledge of the topic can be supported by body language suited to the context.
It is better never to use gestures, to avoid any mistakes.
Only words matter; gestures never influence how a message is understood.

activities.prompt: During a school exchange, Nerea wants to ask a classmate to wait without interrupting the teacher. Which non-verbal signal is most polite here?
activities.explanation: A gentle open-palm gesture can ask someone to wait without disturbing the lesson.
activities.hint: Choose the option that respects both the teacher and the classmate.
options: Suddenly standing up and repeatedly pointing at the classroom clock.
Making a loud hissing sound in front of the whole class.
Gently showing an open palm and giving a friendly look.

activities.prompt: What role do emojis and emoticons play in digital chat messages?
activities.explanation: They can complement written words with feelings and intentions, much as gestures and tone do in spoken conversation.
options: They are compulsory decorations that decide whether a sentence is simple or compound.
They are foreign words that replace spelling rules.
They are non-verbal graphics that add emotion, tone and shades of meaning to written text.
